title: Parse measurements into finite millimetres
description: Parse bounded fractional imperial, decimal imperial, and metric source input into finite millimetre values while retaining the user's display-unit preference.
acceptanceCriteria: Metric decimal input parses to finite millimetres
Decimal imperial input converts using exactly 25.4 millimetres per inch
Common whole-plus-fraction and fraction-only imperial input parses without evaluation or executable code
Zero denominators, excessive fraction size, malformed text, NaN, and infinity return structured parse errors
Equivalent metric and imperial source values normalize equivalently within documented numeric precision
Changing display preference does not mutate normalized geometry

steps.details: Create a pure result type containing either a finite millimetre value plus source disclosure or a structured error code, field reference, and corrective message.
Parse trimmed decimal text with explicit unit selection, reject non-finite output, and convert inches using the documented 25.4 constant.
Parse signed whole, numerator, and denominator tokens directly; cap token length and magnitude, reject zero denominator, and never use `eval` or dynamic code.
Store display-unit preference separately from normalized millimetres and format source disclosures without feeding formatted rounding back into calculations.
Add table-driven checks for metric, decimal inch, mixed fraction, fraction-only, malformed, zero-denominator, overflow, and equivalent-unit cases.

technicalNotes: Geometry parsing must remain pure and import no React, DOM, storage, or PDF APIs.
Formatting precision is a presentation concern and must not silently round durable geometry.
